primary_meaning: Human efforts or deeds of obedience to the Mosaic Law (Torah) that cannot justify or make a person righteous before God, in contrast to justification by faith in Christ

alternatives.meaning: Jewish ethnic boundary markers or identity badges (circumcision, food laws, Sabbath observance) rather than the Torah as a whole or general moral effort
basis: New Perspective on Paul scholarship (Sanders, Dunn, Wright)

alternatives.meaning: Primarily the ceremonial/ritual prescriptions of the Mosaic Law (as distinct from its moral requirements), so that moral good works remain relevant under grace
basis: Historical Catholic and some Protestant readings of Romans/Galatians

alternatives.meaning: Any human works or self-reliant efforts in general (not limited to Mosaic Law) that attempt to earn standing with God
basis: Broader Reformation-era extensions of Romans 3–4 and Galatians

notes: The phrase is almost exclusively Pauline. Traditional Protestant teaching (still dominant in many churches) treats it as law-keeping that fails to justify. Academic biblical studies commonly favor the New Perspective boundary-marker reading. Catholic and some historical Protestant views often narrow it to ceremonial aspects. Ongoing debates mean no single settled interpretation exists across Christian traditions and scholarship.
